decisions.reason: As a newly launched extension of the established laser-marking offer, it is strategically close to existing capabilities and customers, and absent clear evidence of performance below aspiration levels a large incumbent with some slack would usually keep it while learning, though its more niche manual workstation role raises some risk.

This thermal inkjet printer sits very close to the core coding and marking business, uses the firm’s existing development, service and sales resources, and with no visible shortfall against aspirations the firm would likely retain it during the early market-validation phase.

The piezo inkjet printer also fits the established product-market domain and Industry 4.0 direction, so under bounded rationality and normal organisational slack management would tend to keep it unless results clearly disappointed, although technical and market uncertainty make it slightly riskier than the thermal inkjet model.
